cases.scenario_match: an area G op of graphlet_summary, graphlet_walks, graphlet_walk, graphlet_labels or graphlet_compare whose arguments send max_bytes above 262,144 and at most 16,777,216 (DESIGN-v8 §5: 262,145), refused on the MCP way (W3) and answered by the library ways (W1, W2, W4)

direct_expectation.behaviour: the library ways (GraphletTools at the deployed library_commit, configured from the capabilities' graphlet.library block) accept any int max_bytes in [64, 16,777,216] and answer the call as usual: a page of at most that many bytes (a longer list pages with next_cursor); no HTTP is involved

service_answer.detail: The MCP tool forwards max_bytes unchanged in the loopback body of POST /traverse/graphlets/{handle}/<op> (app/mcp_server.py:8149-8170; compare app/mcp_server.py:8410-8450: FastMCP accepts any int for `max_bytes: int | None`). The route refuses it in _max_bytes BEFORE the handle is authorised or any op is enqueued (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:404-415, called at :709 and, for compare, :871): HTTP 422 (bad_argument is a library code: app/traversal/ops_contract.py:465), detail {code: bad_argument, message: 'max_bytes: an int in [64, 262144]; for the complete answer use graphlet_export'}. The tool error is {error: {code: bad_argument, message}} (app/mcp_server.py:8084 -> _traverse_err app/mcp_server.py:6953): no field, no retryable, no other key. The ceiling 262,144 is the code constant ops_contract.MAX_MAX_BYTES (app/traversal/ops_contract.py:226; no setting; the answer is pickled into the queue Redis). Order: after the gate, the handle's UUID form, the token's presence and the junk guards (MCP app/mcp_server.py:8151-8166; REST app/api/routes_graphlets.py:705-708), before the token is checked against the job (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:711 -> :471-482): a wrong_token or bad_handle probe must not also send max_bytes > 262,144. The error is fitted to 2048 bytes (an invalid max_bytes reads as the default: ops_contract.error_ceiling, app/traversal/ops_contract.py:541-551); it fits (124 bytes as the MCP error). The worker refuses such a request too, with another text ('max_bytes: at most 262144; ...', app/traversal/ops_runtime.py:620-622), unreachable through the route. Not covered: graphlet_sequence and graphlet_export take no max_bytes on either side (no MCP parameter; the library's methods answer bad_argument for an unknown keyword), so a plan never sends it there.

A model larger than the store's max_ram_mb (512) is parsed on demand instead of kept resident: slower, the same answer

service_answer.tool: graphlet_walks | graphlet_walk | graphlet_sequence | graphlet_labels | graphlet_compare | graphlet_export

service_answer.detail: The route reads the ref row (no op is enqueued, nothing is parsed). walks, walk, sequence, labels: _prepare_op -> _require_body(in_service=True) (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:598-608, :503-524): 409 (app/traversal/ops_contract.py:474) {code: body_too_large, message: 'this graphlet's body (<n> bytes) is above the in-service ceiling (8388608 bytes): only graphlet_summary and graphlet_export(format=mgt) serve it', handle, body_bytes, max_body_bytes 8388608, in_service_reason body_too_large, download, hint}. compare: the same for a, then for b, with side 'a' | 'b' (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:618-619). export fasta | gfa | json: after its argument checks (ops_exports.normalize_export_args, app/traversal/ops_exports.py:301-341: a bad format / arm / walks is refused first), ops_exports.export_refusal (app/traversal/ops_exports.py:391-400, via request_export :564-566 and the route :912-930, :1042): 409 {code: body_too_large, message: 'this graphlet's body is above the in-service ceiling (TRAVERSAL_INSERVICE_MAX_BODY_MB): no local op runs on it; graphlet_export format='mgt' gives its download link', body_bytes, download, hint}; body_too_large comes before the json / gfa 512 KiB gates (op_memory), so it is never op_memory here; no export row is written. The MCP tool keeps every field (app/mcp_server.py:8084); the tools with max_bytes fit the error to the call's ceiling (default 2048; the message is cut first, then the largest fields, download first; the code is never cut: app/traversal/ops_contract.py:581-607, app/mcp_server.py:8126-8137); sequence's ceiling is 16384; export's error is not fitted. Order: the gate, the handle, the junk guards and a max_bytes outside [64, 262144] (graphlet.max_bytes_above_service_cap) come first, then the job (404 unknown_handle / 410 job_expired), the token (403 forbidden), then no_graphlet / body_deleted, then body_too_large. The ceiling: in_service = body_bytes <= TRAVERSAL_INSERVICE_MAX_BODY_MB x 2^20, set when the body is stored (app/traversal/mgt.py:282-287, app/traversal/execute.py:2025-2027; app/settings.py:1551-1553). Worker backstops, unreachable through the route: app/traversal/ops_runtime.py:255-257 and app/traversal/ops_store.py:273-277 (body_too_large {body_bytes, hint}). What the service still serves for such a handle: graphlet_summary from the row (graphlet.body_over_in_service_ceiling.summary) and graphlet_export format mgt: 200 {export_id: null, format: mgt, status: done, handle, link, bytes, gz_bytes, in_service: false} (app/traversal/ops_exports.py:424-450, app/api/routes_graphlets.py:933-948), which is W4's input.

service_answer.detail: _prepare_op checks the row only (_require_body(in_service=False): no_graphlet / body_deleted) and answers _row_summary without parsing or enqueueing anything (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:598-605, :559-595): 200 {handle, delivery: inline, in_service: false, in_service_reason: body_too_large, body_bytes, max_body_bytes: 8388608, download, note, summary | summary_trimmed}, held to max_bytes (default 2048; the first candidate that fits: full summary, its core, the frame alone; result_too_large when not even the frame fits). It carries NO evidence block. detail and cursor are ignored (detail limitations also answers the row frame, no rows / total; a cursor is never checked); arm narrows summary.arms (a string that is no arm alias: bad_arm 422; an arm the graphlet lacks: empty arms, where the library answers bad_arm). The MCP tool relays the body unchanged (app/mcp_server.py:8177-8208; its docstring names only {handle, summary, delivery, in_service, in_service_reason, download}). The positive service check in_service (graphlet_service_checks.check_in_service) reads in_service false + download on the same answers. UNSURE: whether the full stored summary fits 2048 next to the presigned link (about 1.1 KB): plans should send max_bytes 262144 on this op to compare the stored summary, else expect summary_trimmed.

service_answer.detail: POST /traverse/graphlets/{handle}/export with format mgt (also the default when format is absent: app/api/routes_graphlets.py:1031-1032) is answered by the API itself: normalize_export_args (app/traversal/ops_exports.py:301-341; arm / walks with mgt -> bad_argument :320-322, what -> bad_argument :318-319), then, after authorisation, _mgt_answer (app/api/routes_graphlets.py:933-948, :1038-1041) -> ops_exports.mgt_answer (app/traversal/ops_exports.py:424-450): export_refusal for mgt checks only unknown_handle / no_graphlet / body_deleted (:381-390: no in-service check, no export gate), and results.body_link (app/traversal/results.py:728-756) presigns the stored object (unknown_handle {reason: job_expired} when the job has no life left for a link). No op, no traversal_exports row, no parse, no worker, any body size. 200 {export_id: null, format: mgt, status: done, handle, link, bytes, gz_bytes, in_service} exactly: no records, no path, no fields_cut. The MCP tool relays it unchanged (status done: no collect_note / retry_note; app/mcp_server.py:8453-8525). The stored object is gzip(mgt.standalone_text(body, result, response)) (app/traversal/execute.py:1890, :1905): H + J + the server body + Z, byte for byte the library's dump(from_response(...), envelope=True) for a canonical body (app/traversal/mgt.py:10-15); bytes = mgt.body_digest's count of the server body (app/traversal/execute.py:1896, app/traversal/mgt.py:275-279), gz_bytes the stored gzip size (app/traversal/execute.py:1905-1910). Excused on W3-W4 and W3-W5: the receipt's records (absent on W3), path (absent on W3; also an ENV_KEY the suite drops), export_id null, format, status, handle, link, gz_bytes, in_service (W3's receipt-only keys: service fields) and bytes' other meaning (an ENV_KEY). NOT excused: the file. FORMAT v2 B3 compares it by content (file_view: mgt by its body digest, H seed_index masked, J and Z out): W3's file is the stored body, so its body digest equals W4's document (the MCP's exported .mgt.gz, arms/mcp/docs/<scenario>.mgt.gz) and W1's after standalone_text, which the pre-check's body digest (W1 = W2 = W4) covers. Caution, suite at 1556ec439: compare_records reads a W3 pair's file view only when the receipts agree (compare_graphlets.py:688-693) and a verified case excuses the whole W3-W4 / W3-W5 pair of kind answer (graphlet_service_checks.py:58-60, :460): with this case W3's own downloaded mgt file is not compared on those pairs, only through the pre-check (W4's document is the same stored object).
